whyThisShow: This one is officially out in the world — it was released as part of "In and Out of the Garden: Madison Square Garden '81, '82, '83," so the band's organization put their stamp on it. The Half Step > Franklin's Tower opener draws the most attention, with multiple listeners calling it out as the anchor of the first set. One reviewer said "Jerry is 'on' tonight is what it comes down to". The Lazy Lightning > Supplication stretch in set two pulls particular notice for its balance of structure and freedom, described as having "the improvisational beauty that is more associated with the early days". Set two closes through He's Gone, The Other One, Stella Blue, and Brokedown Palace — a sequence one listener called "very sweet" and "well deserving a Brokedown".
listenFor: The Half Step > Franklin's Tower pairing is what reviewers come back to first. One listener caught "some pretty crunchy... accidental feedback during Half-Step" and flagged it as part of the texture of the night. The Scarlet > Fire draws attention for a structural oddity — one reviewer noted it "ends with the lack of the coda jam at the end and instead has a twilighting sort of 'about to play comes a time or saint stephen' sort of sound" before moving into Sailor > Saint. On the board source, one reviewer noted Brent's keyboard sound is worth tracking from the opening bars of Scarlet: "Scarlet-Fire is 5 star from Brent's great keyboard sound on the opening bars of scarlet through jerry going nuts on the last jam in fire".
context: This is a soundboard recording sourced from the Miller collection (gd1981-03-10.sbd.miller.115598.flac16), and sound quality draws consistent praise. The show was later officially released as part of "In and Out of the Garden: Madison Square Garden '81, '82, '83," the box set documenting the band's run at MSG across three years. By 1981 Brent Mydland had been in the band for two years, and one reviewer noted that around this period "by '82 you can hear how he becomes an integral part of the band". MSG was a regular stop the band treated as a home venue on the East Coast.
funFact: One listener flagged a loud noise at the top of the show and wanted it on record: "THAT LOUD NOISE IN THE BEGINNING OF THE FIRST SONG THAT WASN'T A MISTAKE ,,,THAT WAS ART!!!".
headline: MSG, March '81, Half Step first.
